title: Staged Multi-Agent Training for Human-Exoskeleton Co-Adaptation: Simulation-Based Learning and Real-World Metabolic and Biomechanical Validation
abstract: arXiv:2608.00715v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Learning-based controllers can enable exoskeleton assistance to be trained entirely in physics-based simulation, but achieving effective assistance on real users remains challenging because the human and device continuously adapt to one another. We investigate a Staged Multi-Agent Training (SMAT) approach that jointly trains a musculoskeletal human actor and a bilateral hip-exoskeleton actor (control policy) to learn coordinated assistance strategies while accounting for human-device co-adaptation. The resulting policy was transferred to a physical hip exoskeleton and evaluated in eight healthy adults across users and locomotion conditions without subject-specific retraining. Indirect calorimetry was used to compare no-exoskeleton, passive, and active conditions. Active assistance reduced net metabolic rate by 19.7% relative to the passive device (p < 0.001). translated_title: 面向人-外骨骼协同适应的分阶段多智能体训练：基于仿真的学习与真实世界代谢及生物力学验证
translated_abstract: 基于学习的控制器可以使外骨骼辅助策略完全在基于物理的仿真中进行训练，但由于人体与设备会持续相互适应，在真实用户身上实现有效的辅助仍然具有挑战性。我们研究了一种分阶段多智能体训练（SMAT）方法，该方法联合训练一个肌肉骨骼人类执行者和一个双侧髋部外骨骼执行者（控制策略），从而在考虑人-设备协同适应的前提下学习协调一致的辅助策略。所得到的策略被迁移到实体髋部外骨骼上，并在八名健康成年人中跨用户和运动条件进行了评估，无需针对特定受试者进行重新训练。研究采用间接量热法比较了无外骨骼、被动和主动三种条件。主动辅助相较于被动设备使净代谢率降低了19.7%（p < 0.001）。该策略产生的髋部机械功率以正值为主。
tldr: 该论文提出分阶段多智能体训练（SMAT）方法，在仿真中联合训练肌肉骨骼人类模型与髋部外骨骼控制策略以实现人-机协同适应，并在无需受试者特异性重训练的情况下，于真实用户中验证了主动辅助可使净代谢率较被动设备降低19.7%。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a Staged Multi-Agent Training (SMAT) approach that jointly trains a musculoskeletal human model and a hip-exoskeleton control policy in simulation to achieve human-exoskeleton co-adaptation, validated in real-world experiments showing 19.7% metabolic reduction compared to a passive device without subject-specific retraining.
